claim.why_it_matters: The content is present, so nothing normative is lost, but the display form is. In printed RELEASE general rule 4a the qualifier "according to the rules specified for the MOVE statement" is a standalone paragraph governing BOTH alternative MOVE statements; flattened onto the `or` line it reads as qualifying only the literal-1 alternative. The transcription renders the identical construct correctly for REWRITE on page 742 (MOVE line / `or` / MOVE line / qualifier, each on its own line), so this page contradicts the file's own convention.

verdict.reasoning:
Both source quotations check out, but the difference is page-break furniture plus line-flattening, with zero content change.

WHAT I INDEPENDENTLY OBSERVED.

Rendered PDF page 734 (printed folio 704) at 300 dpi. Its last content is RELEASE general rule 4, and the page ends mid-rule with three display elements and then simply stops:
    a)   The statement:
            MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1
                  or
(footer: 704  (C)ISO/IEC 2023). The rule 4a construct is severed by the page break immediately after the standalone centered "or".

Rendered PDF page 735 (printed folio 705) at 300 dpi. It opens exactly as the claim states: a sans-serif display line "MOVE literal-1 TO record-name-1", then a separate serif paragraph "according to the rules specified for the MOVE statement.", then "b)  The same RELEASE statement without the FROM phrase.", then the NOTE, then general rules 5) and 6). The claim's characterization of the PDF is accurate.

Markdown, specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 29918-29932. The page-734 slice ends:
      MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1

      or MOVE literal-1 TO record-name-1 according to the rules specified for the MOVE statement.
and the page-735 slice then begins at "b) The same RELEASE statement without the FROM phrase." The claim's characterization of the markdown is also accurate, verbatim.

WHY THIS IS NOT A CONTENT DISCREPANCY.

1) Nothing is missing, added, reordered, or altered. Every word of both printed elements is present, in printed order, inside the correct rule (14.9.32.4 general rule 4a), attached to the correct "a) The statement:" lead-in, and still followed by "b)". The claim itself concedes "nothing normative is lost." This is the textbook definition of a line-wrapping / display-form difference, which the rejection criteria list explicitly.

2) The page-slice assignment is page-break furniture. The two elements print on folio 705 but sit in the page-734 slice because the transcription pulled the orphaned tail of a severed rule back across the boundary to keep rule 4a contiguous. That is boundary bookkeeping, not content relocation between different rules or sections. The reader reaches the same text at the same point in the same rule.

3) The alleged meaning change does not survive scrutiny. The claim asserts that flattening makes the qualifier read as governing only the literal-1 alternative. But (a) the sentence's subject is "The statement:", so "according to the rules specified for the MOVE statement" modifies the whole disjunction regardless of line breaks; (b) both alternatives ARE literal MOVE statements, so 14.9.25 MOVE general rules apply to each by definition -- the qualifier is a restatement, and there is no reading on which the identifier-1 alternative escapes the MOVE rules; (c) syntax rule 3 on page 734 independently binds both operands ("Identifier-1 or literal-1 shall be valid as a sending operand in a MOVE statement specifying record-name-1 as the receiving operand"); and (d) the NOTE on page 735 itself invokes "14.9.25, MOVE statement, general rules" specifically for the identifier-1 case. No implementer obligation differs between the two renderings.

4) Flattening printed lines into one logical line is this file's dominant convention, not a violation of it. On page 735 alone, the NOTE, general rule 5 and general rule 6 are each reflowed from 3-4 printed lines into a single markdown line. The transcription makes no promise to preserve printed line breaks in prose.

5) The "contradicts its own convention" argument is factually correct but is a cosmetic style variance, and its cause confirms rather than undermines the refutation. Surveying all three occurrences of the qualifier in the file: line 30186 (REWRITE GR 7a, page 742) and line 33106 both render it standalone; only line 29923 (RELEASE GR 4a) is flattened. The distinguishing feature of the RELEASE instance is precisely that it straddles a page break, while the REWRITE instance sits entirely within page 742. The inconsistency is therefore a direct artifact of the page-boundary merge -- i.e. page-break furniture -- rather than an independent transcription error.

On the rejection criteria: the "missing" text is present; the difference is page-break furniture and line wrapping; neither source is misquoted; the meaning is unchanged. Rejected.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The claim quotes both sources accurately, but every word of printed page 735's opening display line ("MOVE literal-1 TO record-name-1") and its following qualifier paragraph ("according to the rules specified for the MOVE statement.") is present in specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 29923, in printed order, within the correct rule (14.9.32.4 GR 4a) and still followed by item b). The only differences are (i) the transcription pulled the tail of a page-break-severed rule back into the page-734 slice so rule 4a stays contiguous, and (ii) it flattened three printed display lines into one markdown line -- the same reflowing it applies to the NOTE and GRs 5 and 6 on this very page. The asserted semantic drift (qualifier scoped to only the literal-1 alternative) does not occur: the sentence subject is "The statement:", both alternatives are MOVE statements to which 14.9.25 applies by definition, syntax rule 3 independently binds both operands, and the page-735 NOTE explicitly invokes the MOVE general rules for the identifier-1 case. The observed inconsistency with the REWRITE rendering on page 742 is real but cosmetic, and its cause is the page-break merge itself: of the three occurrences of this qualifier in the file (lines 29923, 30186, 33106), only the one straddling a page boundary is flattened. If any action is ever wanted it is a pure formatting touch-up -- split line 29923 into "or" / "MOVE literal-1 TO record-name-1" / qualifier and move the last two into the page-735 slice -- with no change to normative content and no compiler impact.
